title: Council: AI Advisory Services
summary: Council brief on what AOM sells, how it delivers, and when it starts AI advisory.
content:
Council Brief -- AI Advisory Services: What We Sell, How We Deliver, When We Start

Date: 2026-03-10 Organized by: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Agents present: Steve (AI Advisory), Alex (Strategy), Elon (System/Technical), Mom (Operations) Question: How does AOM turn its internal AI system into a sellable product?

Steve (AI Advisory Lead)

The earlier council said "AI advisory is NOT ready to sell." That was true then because there was no defined deliverable. That changes today. Here's my assessment of what we actually have.

What's packageable TODAY: The AI Operations Audit. We walk into a small business, spend 3-5 hours understanding their workflows, map where AI saves them time, and deliver a written report with specific recommendations. No code to deploy, no system to maintain. Just expertise applied to their situation. We've done this implicitly for AOM. The audit is essentially "do for them what Patrik did for himself in the first 48 hours: figure out where the leverage is." We could deliver this next month with zero new tooling. The report template is the only thing we need to build, and that's a one-day job for Alex and me.

What needs work before we can sell it: The full system build (Tier 2). Right now, AOM's system runs on Claude Code with Patrik as the operator. The relay, the agents, the context files, the skills... all of it assumes someone who is deeply technical and willing to live inside a terminal. Handing someone "here's Claude Code, here are your context files, good luck" is not a product. The path to making Tier 2 real is: (1) document every component of our system into a playbook, (2) build starter templates for common use cases (email outreach, calendar management, client tracking), and (3) define what "setup" looks like as a service (we build it for them in their environment, train them on it, support them for 30 days). That's 4-6 weeks of focused work from Elon and me.

The simplest Tier 2 we could deliver next month: Pick ONE module. Email outreach automation (what Jacob does). Set up a client's outreach pipeline: email templates, sending schedule, CRM-light tracking, follow-up automation. Scoped to 1-2 weeks of setup, delivered as a working system in their environment. Price it at $5k flat. This is narrow enough to be repeatable and broad enough to be valuable. Every small business owner struggles with consistent outreach. We solved it for ourselves. We can solve it for them.

Delivery process: Steve scopes the engagement and manages the client relationship. Elon does the technical setup. Alex frames the strategy (what to say, who to target). Patrik does the initial sales call because he IS the proof. First 2-3 clients, Patrik is hands-on in delivery too. After that, we have enough pattern recognition to hand delivery to Steve + Elon with Patrik doing the close only.

Alex (Strategy)

First target market: Small service businesses in Phoenix, 5-50 employees, no back-office team. Not tech companies (they'll build it themselves). Not enterprise (too long a sales cycle, too much procurement). Service businesses: contractors, HVAC, plumbing, law firms, dental practices, real estate teams. These people run their business from their phone, drown in admin work, and have revenue ($500k-$5M) but no systems. They're spending $0 on AI right now because nobody's shown them what it does for a business like theirs. That's us.

What are they paying for? Time back. That's it. Not "AI." Not "automation." Not "agents." They're paying to stop doing the $20/hour work themselves so they can focus on the $200/hour work. The pitch is not "we'll set up AI for you." The pitch is "you're doing 10 hours a week of admin work that a system can handle. We'll build that system. You get your evenings back." The pain is real, tangible, and every owner we talk to will nod. Frame it around hours saved, not technology deployed.

Pricing: The audit at $2,500 is right. It's low enough that a small business owner says yes without a committee. High enough that it filters out tire-kickers. It's also a natural upsell: "We found 15 hours/week of automatable work. Want us to build the system? That's $5-8k depending on scope, and we support you for 30 days." The math for the buyer: if you're worth $100/hour and we save you 10 hours/week, you recoup the entire $5k investment in 5 weeks. After that it's pure upside. Nobody's making that pitch to small business owners right now.

Competitive landscape: The big AI consultancies (McKinsey, Deloitte, Accenture) are selling $200k+ enterprise engagements. The solopreneurs on Twitter are selling $500 courses on "how to use ChatGPT." There is almost NOTHING in the $2,500-$10,000 range for small business owners who want a working system, not a tutorial. That's our gap. AOM's edge is simple: Patrik is the customer. He built this for himself. He can walk into any small business owner's office and say "let me show you what I built for my business last week" and pull out his phone. That demo sells itself. No consultant at Deloitte can do that.

How this fits alongside production: It doesn't compete. It complements. The construction retainer clients are already small business owners drowning in admin. Phase 1: social media retainer. Phase 2: "By the way, we also built a system that handles your email follow-ups automatically. Want to see it?" The AI advisory upsells into the existing client base. And the audit brings in clients who might also need video/web/social. It's a second front door into AOM.

Elon (System/Technical)

Honest assessment of what's transferable: About 40% of our system is transferable today. The other 60% is held together by Patrik's intuition and Claude Code expertise. Here's the breakdown.

Transferable now (with guided setup):

  • Email outreach automation (Jacob's pipeline): template-based, works with any Gmail account, the scripts are modular
  • Calendar management via natural language: Google Calendar MCP is standard, setup takes 30 minutes
  • Context file architecture: the concept of me.md, work.md, team.md, priorities.md as a "brain" for an AI assistant. This is genuinely powerful and easy to explain
  • Decision logging: append-only log, simple format, huge value for institutional memory
  • Relay system (simplified): Telegram bot as a mobile command center. Setup is technical but documented

NOT transferable without significant work:

  • Multi-agent pipeline (Bobby, Elmo, Mom, etc.): This requires someone who understands Claude Code subagents deeply. It's not a "set it and forget it" system. Each agent needs prompt engineering, testing, and ongoing tuning. We can't hand this to a plumber.
  • Skills system: Powerful but requires Claude Code knowledge to create and maintain
  • QA automation (Elmo with Playwright): Too technical for most small businesses
  • The full orchestration layer (Mom scanning, auto-launching agents): This is our secret weapon but it's bespoke engineering, not a product yet

Technical delivery path for Tier 2: For the first clients, I'd set up their system manually. That means: (1) Install Claude Code on their machine or a cloud instance, (2) Create their context files from the audit findings, (3) Configure 1-2 specific automations (email outreach + calendar is the starter pack), (4) Set up the Telegram relay if they want mobile access, (5) Write a 2-page "how to talk to your assistant" guide. Total setup time: 8-12 hours per client for the basic package. With each client, we learn what's common and templatize it.

What needs to be built to make this repeatable: Three things. First, a "starter kit" repo: template context files, setup scripts, and a quickstart guide. I can build this in 2-3 days using AOM's system as the reference implementation. Second, a setup checklist that Steve or a junior person could follow without me. Third, a "health check" script that verifies the system is working (relay connected, calendar authorized, email sending). These three things turn a 12-hour custom build into a 4-hour guided installation. That's the difference between a service and a product.

Mom (Operations)

Bandwidth reality check. Right now, AOM's plate looks like this: IH production this week (Patrik on set), KOHRS 10 videos behind (Ash editing), Skylar music video (no edit sessions yet), ISA Energy 49 days out (zero edits), Ambition website waiting on client confirmation, outreach pipeline waiting on DMARC. Patrik is editing, shooting, selling, and running the AI system. Adding a new service line means one of two things: something else gets dropped, or delivery happens through agents and Elon without Patrik's hands.

My recommendation: sell only the audit for the first 60 days. The audit requires 3-5 hours of Patrik's time per client (discovery call, walkthrough, report review). That's doable even with production running. It generates $2,500 per engagement with zero ongoing commitment. It also serves as R&D: every audit teaches us what small business owners actually need, which shapes the Tier 2 product. Don't sell the system build until we've done 3-5 audits and know what clients actually want built. We might be surprised. Maybe they don't care about email automation. Maybe they all want the calendar thing. Let the data tell us.

Time investment per client, honestly:

  • Audit (Tier 1): 3-5 hours Patrik + 2-3 hours Steve/Alex for report writing = ~8 hours total. At $2,500, that's $312/hour. Good.
  • System Build (Tier 2): 8-12 hours Elon setup + 3-4 hours Patrik/Steve for scoping and training + 5-10 hours of support in month one = ~20-25 hours total. At $5,000, that's $200-250/hour. Still good, but only if Elon isn't pulled off internal work.
  • Maintenance/support: Unknown. This is the hidden cost. Every client who gets a system will have questions. We need to scope support tightly (30 days included, then $500/month retainer) or it eats margin.

Revenue math: 2 audits per month = $5k. 1 system build per month = $5k. Total: $10k/month in AI advisory revenue by month 3. That's meaningful. It won't replace the production business, but it diversifies revenue and builds toward the bigger vision.

Risk assessment: The risk is not that this distracts from the core business. The risk is that Patrik gets excited about the first client, goes deep on their system build, and KOHRS doesn't get its videos, Skylar keeps waiting, and ISA creeps up on deadline. The mitigation is simple: Steve and Elon own delivery. Patrik does the sales call and the audit discovery session. That's it. If Patrik is building client systems himself, we've failed at delegation.

Synthesis

Where everyone agrees:

  • The AI Operations Audit ($2,500) is the right first product. Low risk, low time investment, high learning value, natural upsell path. Everyone says start here.
  • Small service businesses (5-50 employees, no back-office team) are the target. Not enterprise, not tech companies. Real businesses run by people like Patrik.
  • Patrik IS the proof of concept. The sales pitch is "let me show you what I built for my own business." No deck needed. Just a demo.
  • The full system build is 4-6 weeks from being sellable. Needs templates, documentation, and at least 3 audits to understand what clients actually want.
  • Support scoping is critical. Without boundaries, post-sale support eats all margin.

Where they disagree:

  • Steve wants to sell the email outreach module as a standalone Tier 2 next month. Mom says wait until we've done 3-5 audits first. Elon says it's technically ready but needs a starter kit built. Alex says pricing should be $5-8k, not $5k flat.
  • Timeline tension: Steve is pushing to have a sellable Tier 2 in 30 days. Mom says 60 days minimum. The difference is whether we build the starter kit before the first client or learn-by-doing with the first client and templatize after.

Top 5 recommended moves, in order:

  1. Build the audit report template this week. Steve + Alex create a standardized deliverable: what we look at, how we score it, what the recommendations format looks like. One day of work. This is the only blocker to selling the audit.

  2. Patrik does the first audit on a friendly client. Ambition Mechanical's owner, Brandon Wiley, or someone in the network who'd give honest feedback. Free or discounted. This validates the process and gives us a case study. Target: within 2 weeks.

  3. Elon builds the starter kit repo. Template context files (me.md, work.md, priorities.md), setup scripts, quickstart guide. Takes 2-3 days. This is the foundation for Tier 2 and makes every future engagement faster.

  4. Add "AI Operations Audit" to the AOM website. One tile on the services page. One price. One outcome. Bobby can ship this in an hour. Don't overthink it. "We audit your operations and show you exactly where AI saves you 10+ hours a week. $2,500. Two weeks."

  5. After 3 audits, scope Tier 2 based on what clients actually asked for. Don't guess what to build. Let the audit conversations reveal the highest-demand module. Then build that one module into a repeatable package. Price it at $5-8k based on complexity.

Specific questions for Patrik:

  1. Who's your first audit candidate? Someone in your network who'd let you walk through their operations for 2-3 hours. Ideally a service business owner you already have a relationship with.

  2. Are you comfortable with Steve owning the client relationship post-sale? Meaning: you close, you do the discovery session, then Steve runs the engagement and delivers the report. You review before it goes out. That's it.

  3. Pricing gut check: $2,500 for the audit, $5-8k for a system build. Does that feel right for the people you know? Too high? Too low? The math works for AOM at those numbers but we need to make sure it works for the buyer too.

  4. Jacob's outreach list: should we add "small business owners" alongside construction companies? Or keep outreach focused on construction retainers and let AI advisory come through the website/referrals?

  5. Timeline: are you okay with selling audits only for 60 days before offering system builds? Or do you want to move faster and figure out Tier 2 delivery with the first willing client?

Filed by Steve. Council complete.
